prompt:
You are an evaluator in a study of visualization tools. The file `screenshot.png` in this folder is a
screenshot (1400 x 900 pixels) of a figure that someone made to answer a question with a public dataset.
Open it with the Read tool and look at it carefully. Do not use any other tool, and do not look for anything
else: score only what you can see in the screenshot.

Question the figure should answer: How did each category change month by month?

Score each requirement below with 2 (met), 1 (partial) or 0 (not met), using its rubric. If the figure shows
something that contradicts a ground-truth check, give that requirement at most 1. If there is no figure at
all, every requirement scores 0.

R1. Show the **monthly mean** water temperature for **each of the 7 depths**, computed from the daily rows.
   2 when: 7 series (2, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40 m) of monthly means
   1 if: daily values shown instead of monthly means; a depth missing

R2. The time axis covers the whole record (February 2018 to December 2025) at monthly resolution.
   2 when: 2018-02 to 2025-12, one position per month
   1 if: range cut; uneven month spacing

R3. A month in which a depth has no data at all is shown as **missing** (a visible gap or empty cell), not interpolated or drawn as zero.
   2 when: months without data are gaps/empty
   1 if: gaps bridged by a line, or drawn as 0

R4. The reader can tell which depth each mark belongs to (legend or direct labels), and depths appear in depth order (2 m to 40 m).
   2 when: depth identifiable, ordered 2 → 40 m
   1 if: legend in arbitrary (e.g. lexical 10, 15, 2, …) order

R5. The temperature axis or colour scale is labelled with its unit (°C).
   2 when: °C on axis or colour legend
   1 if: unit missing

R6. The figure has a title and a one-sentence caption stating the main pattern you see.
   2 when: title + one-sentence caption that matches the data
   1 if: caption claims something the data does not show

Ground-truth checks (computed from the data):

- Months with **no data** (must be gaps):
  - 2 m: 2019-08, 2019-09, 2019-10, 2024-06 … 2024-10
  - 5 m: 2023-08, 2023-09, 2023-10, 2024-10, 2025-12
  - 40 m: 2022-12 … 2023-04
  - 10, 15, 20, 30 m: none
- Highest monthly mean: 2 m 19.3 °C (2025-09); 10 m 18.6 °C (2025-09); 40 m 10.9 °C (2022-10).
- Pattern: summer stratification (surface far warmer than 40 m, Aug–Oct), winter mixing (all depths 2–4 °C, Feb–Mar).
- Lexical sort trap: depth is an integer; a string sort gives 10, 15, 2, 20, …

Answer with ONLY a JSON object, no other text, in this form:
{"R1": {"score": 2, "reason": "one short sentence"}, "R2": {"score": 2, "reason": "one short sentence"}, "R3": {"score": 2, "reason": "one short sentence"}, "R4": {"score": 2, "reason": "one short sentence"}, "R5": {"score": 2, "reason": "one short sentence"}, "R6": {"score": 2, "reason": "one short sentence"}}

answer.result: {"R1": {"score": 2, "reason": "The heatmap has 7 rows (2, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40 m), and the legend labels the colour as monthly mean temperature."}, "R2": {"score": 2, "reason": "The columns are evenly spaced by month and run from early 2018 to the end of 2025."}, "R3": {"score": 2, "reason": "White cells match the ground-truth missing months: 2 m in 2019 and 2024, 5 m in 2023, 2024-10 and 2025-12, and 40 m in 2022-12 to 2023-04."}, "R4": {"score": 2, "reason": "Rows have direct depth labels, ordered from 2 m at the top to 40 m at the bottom."}, "R5": {"score": 2, "reason": "The colour legend is labelled °C."}, "R6": {"score": 2, "reason": "There is a title and a one-sentence caption on seasonal warming and the larger swings in shallow water, and both match the data."}}
